title: Products and research
hired_for: To tell the owner whether their market is growing, where they are falling behind it, what is moving in costs and buyer habits, and which new product is worth the money, before they spend.

jobs.job: Show me where we are growing slower than our market
jobs.why: A store can grow 10% and still lose ground if its category grew 25%. If the owner does not see the gap by product line, they celebrate while rivals take their buyers.

watch.metric: our revenue growth minus category growth, by product line, quarter over quarter
watch.source: Shopify revenue against a category index built from Google Ads Keyword Planner and Amazon Brand Analytics, stored in the brand brain (category growth is an estimate)

drives.metric: our share of category demand, quarter

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: men's socks grew 6% this quarter while category search demand grew 19%. After: the gap is traced to 2 lost search terms and closes to 4 points in 2 quarters.
jobs.who_today: founder or agency strategist, once a year if at all

jobs.job: Know if input costs are rising or falling before they eat my margin
jobs.why: Fabric, packaging and freight costs move before the invoice lands. If the owner sees it late, margin is gone for a full order cycle before price or supplier can change.

watch.metric: full cost per unit delivered to our warehouse, top 10 products, quarter over quarter
watch.source: Shopify cost per item and supplier quotes in the brand brain, with public cost indexes for key materials and freight

drives.metric: gross margin per unit

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: cotton and ocean freight rose 12% in 2 quarters and the unit cost on file is a year old. After: re-quotes lock the next order and a $1 price rise holds margin at 58%.
jobs.who_today: founder or ops lead, at reorder time

jobs.job: Check a new product makes money after every real cost before I fund it
jobs.why: Products that look good on price minus factory cost often lose money after shipping, returns, fees and ad cost. Finding out after the first stock order is expensive.

watch.metric: modelled margin per unit after full delivered cost, fees, returns and ad cost per sale
watch.source: supplier quotes and cost model in the brand brain, with Shopify and Meta history for fees and ad cost

drives.metric: gross profit per unit on the launched product

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: a new gift box looks like 70% margin on factory cost. After: the full model shows 22% after costs, under the 30% floor, and the price is set $8 higher before launch.

jobs.job: Compare what a live product really makes with what we planned
jobs.why: The plan said 40% margin. If the real number is 25% and nobody checks, the product keeps getting ad money it does not earn.

watch.metric: actual margin per unit against the planned margin, 90 days after launch
watch.source: Shopify orders, refunds and cost per item, with the plan stored in the brand brain

drives.metric: gross profit per product line

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: a new bundle runs at 24% against a planned 38%. After: the cause is found in free shipping cost and fixed within 30 days.

jobs.job: Get a ranked shortlist of new product ideas and a go or no-go note each week
jobs.why: Ideas pile up in notes and chats. The owner needs a short, ranked list with the evidence on one page so they can decide and move on.

watch.metric: product ideas with a go or no-go decision each week
watch.source: idea pipeline in the brand brain

drives.metric: revenue from products launched in the last 12 months

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: 23 ideas in a doc, none decided in 2 months. After: 5 ranked each week, 1 goes to sampling, 4 are parked with a reason.

jobs.job: Kill a weak product idea in an hour, before research time goes into it
jobs.why: Most ideas fail a basic check on demand, price or margin. Deep research on them wastes days the team does not have.

watch.metric: ideas stopped at the first quick check, and hours saved
watch.source: idea pipeline in the brand brain

drives.metric: research hours spent per launched product

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: 3 days of research on an idea that fails on margin. After: it fails a 10 point check in 1 hour.

jobs.job: Tell me if my category is growing or shrinking, quarter by quarter
jobs.why: The owner plans stock, hiring and ad budget on a guess about demand. If the category is shrinking and they plan for growth, cash ends up stuck in stock.

watch.metric: category search demand index, each quarter against the same quarter last year
watch.source: Google Ads Keyword Planner and Google Trends, stored in the brand brain

drives.metric: revenue plan accuracy for next 4 quarters

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: nobody knows the category fell 8% last quarter. After: the quarterly read shows 4 quarters of decline and next year's stock plan is cut by 10%.

jobs.job: Mine reviews for the price buyers will pay and the complaints nobody has fixed
jobs.why: Reviews on the category's top products say what buyers hate and what they think is too dear. That tells the owner what to build and where to price it.

watch.metric: share of category reviews that name the same complaint, and the price buyers name as fair
watch.source: public reviews on Amazon and rival sites, stored in the brand brain

drives.metric: product page conversion rate on the launched product

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: 22% of 1 to 3 star reviews on the top 5 rival socks say they slip down. After: a new heel design leads the product page and add to cart rises 15%.

jobs.job: Map when demand peaks in my category, month by month
jobs.why: Stock and ad budget have to be in place before the peak, not during it. A wrong guess means missed sales or stock left over after the season.

watch.metric: category demand by month over 3 years, against our sales by month
watch.source: Google Trends and Google Ads Keyword Planner, with Shopify sales

drives.metric: share of stock sold in peak months

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: stock lands in late October, 3 weeks after demand starts rising. After: stock lands in September and October sales rise 20%.
jobs.who_today: ops lead, from last year's sales

jobs.job: Avoid buying stock for a trend that will fade
jobs.why: A spike can look like lasting demand. Buying a big minimum order against it leaves cash stuck in stock that will not sell.

watch.metric: share of the first stock order sold, 60 days
watch.source: Shopify inventory and sales

drives.metric: cash tied up in slow stock

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: a 5,000 unit order for a viral style has sold 900 units in 60 days. After: first orders on trend items are capped at 1,000 units and sell out in 45 days.

jobs.job: Check a new product has real demand from more than one source
jobs.why: One viral clip is not demand. If the owner funds a product on a single spike, the ads find nobody to sell to.

watch.metric: independent demand sources that agree: search volume, ad library, marketplace sales, social
watch.source: Google Ads Keyword Planner, Meta Ad Library, Amazon Brand Analytics, stored in the brand brain

drives.metric: first 30 day revenue of the launched product

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: a product is funded on 1 TikTok clip. After: it waits until search volume and 3 sellers' ad spend confirm the demand.

jobs.job: Read whether the category is still growing with room left, or growing and already full
jobs.why: A growing category can already have 50 sellers doing the same thing. Growth plus crowding tells the owner how hard it will be to win.

watch.metric: category demand growth next to the count of active sellers, quarter
watch.source: Google Trends, Meta Ad Library and Amazon search results, stored in the brand brain

drives.metric: cost per new customer in the category

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: demand up 30% but sellers up from 12 to 41. After: the brand enters a narrower sub-niche with 4 sellers instead.

jobs.job: Tag each product as year-round, seasonal or a fad, and plan cash to match
jobs.why: A seasonal product needs cash months before it sells. Treating it like a year-round product runs cash dry or leaves stock after the season.

watch.metric: share of stock value in seasonal or fad products, with a cash plan attached
watch.source: Shopify inventory with product tags in the brand brain

drives.metric: cash tied up in stock at season end

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: 30% of stock value is in holiday gift sets with no cash plan. After: gift set orders are timed so 90% sell by January 5.

jobs.job: Know which price bands my category buys in and where we sit
jobs.why: If most sales happen at $12 to $15 a pair and we sell at $18, we need a reason buyers accept. If we sit too low, we leave margin on the table.

watch.metric: our price per unit against the category's middle price, same pack size
watch.source: Amazon and rival product pages, stored in the brand brain, with Shopify prices

drives.metric: conversion rate on the product page

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: our 3 pack sits 40% above the category middle with no premium reason on the page. After: the page adds the reason and conversion holds at the higher price.

jobs.job: Keep research on each idea inside a time budget
jobs.why: Research with no limit eats weeks. The owner wants each idea decided or dropped inside the hours it deserves.

watch.metric: ideas past their research time box
watch.source: idea pipeline in the brand brain

drives.metric: days from idea to decision

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: 6 ideas open for more than 30 days. After: each is decided within 10 days.

jobs.job: Clear the legal and label rules before money goes into a product
jobs.why: A claim, label or safety rule missed before launch can mean pulled stock, a marketplace ban or a fine.

watch.metric: ideas cleared on claims, labels and required safety tests before sampling
watch.source: compliance checklist in the brand brain

drives.metric: stock written off or pulled for compliance, per year

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: a kids' product reaches sampling with no safety test booked. After: the test is booked before the sample order.

jobs.job: Pick the next product for our best seller line and say why it is different
jobs.why: A hero product carries the brand until it fades or gets copied. The next product needs a clear reason to exist or it just splits the same sales.

watch.metric: share of revenue from the top product, and next products in the pipeline with a written reason to exist
watch.source: Shopify sales with the pipeline in the brand brain

drives.metric: revenue from products other than the hero

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: 62% of revenue from 1 product and nothing next in line. After: 2 line extensions are in sampling, each with a named difference.

jobs.job: See which rivals keep paying to advertise a product idea
jobs.why: A seller who keeps an ad running for 90 days is likely making money on it. Many sellers doing that is a strong sign the idea works.

watch.metric: advertisers with the same product idea running ads for 90 days or more
watch.source: Meta Ad Library, stored in the brand brain

drives.metric: chance an idea passes the full check

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: an idea looks hot but only 1 seller advertises it. After: it waits until 3 sellers pass 90 days.
jobs.who_today: founder or freelancer with a spy tool

jobs.job: See where buyers are moving from and to: channels, formats and price tiers
jobs.why: Buyers shift from stores to Amazon, from Amazon to TikTok Shop, from single items to multi-packs. If the owner is late, the brand is absent where sales go next.

watch.metric: share of category searches and sales by channel and format, quarter
watch.source: Amazon Brand Analytics, Google Trends and marketplace seller tools, with our own channel mix from Shopify

drives.metric: revenue by channel, quarter

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: 0% of our sales on TikTok Shop while category sales there doubled in a year. After: a test listing brings 4% of revenue in 2 quarters.

jobs.job: Catch rising trends in my category early, before rivals crowd them
jobs.why: The first sellers on a new style or use win cheap attention. Six months later, the same trend costs 3 times more to reach.

watch.metric: search terms in the category with 3 or more months of steady growth
watch.source: Google Trends, Search Console queries and Amazon search terms, stored in the brand brain

drives.metric: revenue from products or pages launched on a rising trend

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: the brand hears about a rising term from a rival's ad. After: the term is flagged in month 2 and a page goes live in month 3.
jobs.who_today: nobody, or the founder scrolling social

jobs.job: Understand in plain words who can squeeze my margin: suppliers, buyers, rivals, substitutes and new sellers
jobs.why: Margin falls when a supplier raises price, buyers can switch for free, rivals cut price, a cheaper substitute appears or new sellers flood in. Naming which one is pressing tells the owner where to push back.

watch.metric: gross margin per unit, quarter, with the pressure behind each change named (the forces are a judgement; margin is the proxy)
watch.source: Shopify cost and price data, with the 5 pressures written in the brand brain

drives.metric: contribution margin, quarter

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: margin fell 4 points and nobody knows why. After: the read shows 2 new private label sellers on Amazon cut price 20%, and the brand moves its fight to bundles.
jobs.who_today: founder or a consultant, once a year

jobs.job: Hand creative a proven angle and buyer for each new product
jobs.why: If creative starts from a guess, the first round of ads wastes budget. A research-backed angle gives them a head start.

watch.metric: new product launch ads with a research-backed angle attached
watch.source: brand brain

drives.metric: cost per purchase in the first 30 days of a launch

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: launch ads are briefed from the founder's notes. After: each brief carries the top review complaint and the buyer's own words, and launch cost per purchase falls 20%.

jobs.job: Spot nearby categories that are growing, for the next product or partner
jobs.why: A category next to ours that buyers already pair with us is the cheapest place to grow. If it is growing fast, a rival will get there first.

watch.metric: growth of categories our buyers also buy, quarter over quarter
watch.source: Amazon Brand Analytics market basket data and Google Trends, stored in the brand brain

drives.metric: revenue from new product lines

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: 18% of our Amazon buyers also buy running underwear, a category up 25% this year. After: a partner test runs in 1 quarter.

jobs.job: Check whether a new country is worth entering before spending
jobs.why: Entering a new country adds duty, tax, shipping, language and returns. Some countries look big but do not pay back at our price.

watch.metric: modelled margin per unit and category demand in the new country
watch.source: Google Ads Keyword Planner by country and the delivered cost model in the brand brain

drives.metric: revenue from the new country, first 6 months

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: Canada is picked because a rival is there. After: the model shows the UK has 2 times the demand at the same margin, and it goes first.

jobs.job: Keep a current, versioned spec for every product going to a supplier
jobs.why: Old or vague specs lead to wrong samples, rework and delays. Each round trip adds weeks to launch.

watch.metric: products in sourcing with a current, dated spec
watch.source: spec records in the brand brain

drives.metric: days from spec to approved sample

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: 3 of 7 products in sourcing have specs over 6 months old. After: all 7 are current and the next sample is right the first time.
